<h1>Manifesto for Vibe-Driven<br>Software Development</h1>

<div class="preamble">
We are uncovering better ways of developing<br>
software by prompting for it and seeing what happens.<br>
Through this work we have come to value:
</div>

<div class="values">
<span class="left">Prompts</span> <span class="over">over</span> <span class="right">Plans</span><br>
<span class="left">Instant Gratification</span> <span class="over">over</span> <span class="right">Maintainable Software</span><br>
<span class="left">Velocity</span> <span class="over">over</span> <span class="right">Validity</span><br>
<span class="left">Sleep-in</span> <span class="over">over</span> <span class="right">Stand-Up</span>
</div>

<div class="postscript">
That is, while there is value in the items on<br>
the right, we cannot be bothered with them when<br>
the items on the left feel so productive.
</div>

<div class="page hidden" id="page-principles">
<div class="principles">

<h1>Principles behind the<br>Vibe-Driven Manifesto</h1>

<div class="intro">We follow these principles:</div>

<div class="principle">
Our highest priority is to satisfy the developer<br>
through early and continuous deployment<br>
of whatever Claude just generated.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Welcome changing requirements, even late in<br>
development. Actually, especially late in development,<br>
because we didn't read the requirements at the start.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Deliver deployed software frequently, from a<br>
couple of minutes to a couple of hours, with a<br>
preference to &ldquo;I didn't test this but it compiled.&rdquo;
</div>

<div class="principle">
Business people and developers must work<br>
together daily throughout the project. By &ldquo;work<br>
together&rdquo; we mean the developer shares a Loom<br>
video and the business person reacts with &#x1F525;.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Build projects around motivated individuals.<br>
Give them an API key and a chat window,<br>
and trust them to prompt the job done.
</div>

<div class="principle">
The most efficient and effective method of<br>
conveying information to and within a development<br>
team is a screenshot of a conversation with an AI<br>
posted in Slack without context.
</div>

<div class="principle">
A deployed URL is the primary measure of progress.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Vibe-driven processes promote unsustainable development.<br>
The sponsors, developers, and language models should be<br>
prepared to sprint indefinitely until the demo or the<br>
API credits run out, whichever comes first.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Continuous attention to prompt engineering<br>
and good vibes enhances velocity.<br>
Continuous attention to the codebase is optional.
</div>

<div class="principle">
Simplicity&mdash;the art of maximizing the amount<br>
of code you didn't write and can't explain&mdash;is essential.
</div>

<div class="principle">
The best architectures, requirements, and designs<br>
emerge from a single developer in a flow state<br>
at 2 AM who mass-accepted every Copilot suggestion<br>
and committed without reviewing the diff.
</div>

<div class="principle">
At regular intervals, the team reflects on how<br>
to become more effective, then asks ChatGPT<br>
to summarize the retro and write the action items,<br>
none of which are completed.
</div>

<!-- ABOUT / HISTORY PAGE                    -->

<div class="page hidden" id="page-history">
<div class="history">

<h1>History: The Gathering at<br>Snowbird 2.0</h1>

<p>In February 2024, fifteen developers who had never met in person &mdash; and who, in several cases, had never written a line of code without AI assistance &mdash; gathered at a WeWork in Austin, Texas, to discuss the future of software development.</p>

<p>The original plan was to meet at a ski lodge in Utah, in homage to the original Agile Manifesto authors. The plan was abandoned after three participants could not determine how to book a hotel without asking Claude, and a fourth booked a hotel in Utah, Ohio.</p>

<p>Over the course of two days, the group debated, argued, and ultimately reached consensus on a shared set of values. The debate was vigorous. At one point, Brayden Tokenwindow and Preston Overfit nearly came to blows over whether &ldquo;it works on my machine&rdquo; constitutes a deployment strategy. (The manifesto&rsquo;s position: it does.)</p>

<p>The four values were drafted in a shared Cursor session. The wording was refined through seventeen successive prompts to Claude, each of which began with &ldquo;no, make it sound more like a manifesto.&rdquo; The final version was approved unanimously, deployed to Vercel, and shared on Twitter within forty minutes of being written. It had not been proofread. This was consistent with the values it described.</p>

<p>The Twelve Principles were written the following morning, primarily by Grayson Temperatureknob, who was the only attendee awake before 11 AM. The others approved them via Slack emoji reaction (&#x1F525; constituting a binding vote).</p>

<p>Several principles were debated at length. Principle 7 (&ldquo;A deployed URL is the primary measure of progress&rdquo;) was originally a longer paragraph, but the group agreed that brevity was more consistent with the spirit of vibe-driven development, and also that no one wanted to write the rest of the paragraph.</p>

<p>Principle 11 nearly caused a schism. Stetson Nobackend argued that &ldquo;mass-accepting Copilot suggestions&rdquo; was not a practice to be celebrated. The group voted. Stetson lost 14&ndash;1. He has since updated his LinkedIn to &ldquo;Principled Engineer (Dissenting Signatory).&rdquo;</p>

<p>As of March 2026, the Vibe-Driven Manifesto has been endorsed by over 14,000 signatories, mass-starred on GitHub by 23,000 accounts (approximately 60% of which are bots, which we consider a form of AI endorsement), and cited in four Y Combinator applications, none of which were funded.</p>

<p>The manifesto has been translated into twelve formats, including JSON (lossy), LinkedIn Carousel, and a 47-second TikTok that has more views than the original document. The TikTok is set to a lo-fi hip-hop beat and features the four values appearing one at a time over footage of someone typing in a dark room. It is the definitive version.</p>

<p>The manifesto has not been updated since its publication. Not because it is perfect, but because no one can agree on which AI to use for the revision, and the conversation about it has been moved to a Notion page that no one has opened since.</p>
